cards.summary: This Hawaiian navigation starline organizes bright stars from Capella toward Sirius and Canopus. Nainoa Thompson developed the starline system as a way to remember the sky for ocean navigation.

publication.review: Source-checked against the pinned CC BY-SA Stellarium description, Star Lines and Ke Ka o Makali‘i sections; editorial review, not community endorsement.

cards.summary: This starline connects the northern sky near Polaris and the Big Dipper with Arcturus, Spica, and southern navigation figures. It belongs to the Hawaiian starline system described by navigators and educators in the source.

publication.review: Source-checked against the pinned CC BY-SA description, Ka Iwikuamo‘o section; not community endorsement.

cards.summary: The Great Square of Pegasus forms the central kite in this Hawaiian navigation starline. Its named stars recall chiefs in the account recorded by the source contributors.

publication.review: Source-checked against the pinned CC BY-SA description, Ka Lupe o Kawelo section; not community endorsement.

cards.summary: The Indian Vedic dataset gives the name Dhruva to Polaris. This card records that named-star identification; it does not treat Bengali and Sanskrit terminology as interchangeable.

publication.review: Source-checked against the pinned Indian common_names entry HIP 11767.

cards.summary: Rohiṇī is anchored to Aldebaran in this Vedic sky dataset. The same source distinguishes the visible star figure from the equal divisions used in lunar-mansion systems.

publication.review: Source-checked against Indian index.json Roh and HIP 21421 and description Nakṣatra section.

cards.summary: This Vedic figure joins stars of the Pleiades. Its name and translation are those supplied by the pinned dataset; cultural figures and modern constellation boundaries describe different ways of organizing the sky.

publication.review: Source-checked against the Indian Kṛt constellation entry.
